# Intent MCU Simulator

> Intent MCU Simulator is an original, open-source browser workbench for supported ATmega328P projects, one bounded RP2040 Pico GPIO0/UART0 profile, one bounded ESP32-C3 GPIO2/UART profile, and one bounded STM32F429ZI PB0/USART3 profile.

Canonical application: https://lab.teachthecompany.com/
Source and setup: https://github.com/finnandrehotvedt/intent-mcu-simulator
Licence: Apache-2.0 for project-owned source; third-party components keep their own terms.
Current public version: 1.1.0-rc.17

## Supported public workflow

- Start with an empty project or one of six validated starter projects.
- The thermostat starter compiles the visible source and runs three reset-isolated virtual-time scenarios. Pass requires executed D13, matching UART and complete ordered input evidence; its known-bad equality variant must fail exactly at 30 C.
- In AVR, add any of 16 selectable supported components and connect named pin anchors manually.
- Edit source and compile it through the isolated, fixed AVR toolchain.
- Load and run the accepted artifact in the deterministic virtual MCU worker.
- Inspect GPIO, LEDs, buttons, potentiometers, serial bytes, logic traces, and pin state.
- Save and reopen a project file on the learner's computer; browser recovery is separate.
- Optionally generate a portable Prompt Bridge request and validate returned structured circuit data.
- Select RP2040 Pico, create or reconnect its bounded GP0/resistor/LED/GND cables from named pins, edit the two bounded source values, compile in the fixed isolated Arm toolchain, and run the source-bound UF2 in the browser worker.
- Select ESP32-C3, create or reconnect its bounded GPIO2/resistor/LED/GND cables from named pins, edit only GPIO2 mode/level and an uppercase UART marker, compile a fixed DIO flash image, and run actual Espressif QEMU CPU/UART.
- Select STM32F429ZI, create or reconnect its bounded PB0/resistor/LED/GND cables from named pins, edit the PB0 HIGH/LOW plus uppercase USART3 source values, compile a strict source-bound ELF, and run actual Renode PB0/USART3/reset replay.
- In any narrow controller profile, restore one deleted resistor or LED from Supported parts after Save/Open, then explicitly reconnect its named pins. Add never infers a cable, and Open never restores executable authority.

## Important limits

- The verified teaching profile is a bounded ATmega328P 16 MHz, 5 V subset, not complete hardware equivalence.
- Simulation is not physical safety certification and does not replace testing on suitable physical hardware.
- Prompt Bridge has no hosted AI API or agent/tool connection. It creates portable text for a user-selected tool.
- Free-form AI output cannot draw wires or authorize connections. Only schema-valid, electrically accepted project data reaches the canvas and worker.
- There are no accounts, analytics, advertising, cloud project storage, physical-device uploads, or live AI calls.
- Public execution supports the tested ATmega328P profile, one bounded RP2040 Pico GPIO0/UART0 source profile, one bounded ESP32-C3 GPIO2/UART source profile, and one bounded STM32F429ZI PB0/USART3/reset-replay source profile.
- ESP32-C3 publicly compiles one strict sketch grammar and runs actual QEMU CPU/UART with reset replay. The GPIO2/LED result is a separately labelled project-owned executed-register-write model; QEMU pin state is not observed, and no broad ESP32, SDK, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, timing, or physical-device claim is made.
- RP2040 Pico publicly accepts one exact project-owned C11 grammar, compiles it in a networkless fixed Arm GNU 14.3.1 container, validates a source-bound UF2, and executes GPIO0/UART0 in rp2040js 1.4.0. It does not claim a complete Pico SDK, PIO, DMA, USB, multicore, timing, or physical-device model.
- STM32F429ZI publicly accepts one exact project-owned C11 grammar, compiles it in a fixed networkless Arm GNU 14.3.1 container, validates a source-bound ELF32, and executes PB0/USART3 in actual Renode 1.17.0 across reset replay. Its editable named-pin external LED path remains an ideal teaching circuit; no arbitrary C/ELF, SDK, broad peripheral, timing, physical-board, programming, or full STM32 claim is made.
